details: Bitcoin dropped to around $63,000 on July 28, falling nearly 3% in 24 hours. Investors are exercising caution ahead of the US Federal Reserve's policy meeting on July 29, which is a key macro event. This decline occurred despite some easing of geopolitical tensions, such as a pause in US-Iran military strikes, which had previously led to a brief rally. A technology-led selloff in Asian markets also contributed to the crypto market's downturn, with major altcoins experiencing significant losses.
title: Bitcoin Slides to $63K Amid Fed Caution Despite Easing Geopolitical Tensions

details: On July 23, 2026, the European Union adopted its 21st sanctions package against Russia and Belarus. These new measures significantly expand restrictions on financial infrastructure and crypto-asset channels. The package includes transaction bans on 14 crypto-related service platforms operating across six jurisdictions and establishes a legal framework for potential comprehensive third-country bans on crypto services deemed to be enabling sanctions evasion. This aims to further cripple Russia's ability to fund its war and circumvent existing sanctions.
title: EU Imposes 21st Sanctions Package, Expands Crypto Restrictions on Russia/Belarus

details: Russia's State Duma passed a comprehensive law regulating digital currencies, set to take effect on September 1, 2026. The legislation establishes a legal framework for crypto trading, requiring exchanges, brokers, and service providers to obtain central bank licenses by July 1, 2027. While crypto payments remain prohibited domestically, the law permits their use for cross-border settlements. Retail investors will face annual purchase limits of approximately $3,800 and must pass a knowledge test to trade cryptocurrencies.
title: Russia Legalizes Crypto Trading Under Strict Central Bank Oversight
